source_text: So it was today, I think, that I was starting to look, from the elephant side, Add building up models of collaboration models of collaboration and we talked about generalizing the notion of a click as used by the war machine so that it could describe any episode of multi-agent work like what I've been doing with the M-futon court where Claude 4 might kick off a phase of work with a number of other agents in fact, we were even looking at that as a specific example where sometimes that works or sometimes one of my instructions might have gotten dropped along the way and all of that's really useful stuff to have but I also want to caution that as implemented, the war machine has two agents inside of it and the theory should generalize if possible, but we should keep the implementation simple so that we can get back to running experiments with it but I certainly would love it if we could generalize it further as we go.

reply_text:
㊥ ("the war machine has two agents inside of it") Understood, and the split you describe is already how R11 stands. The Lean statement is for any finite set of agents; the code side will be written only for the two the runner casts, the author and the reviewer.

㊣ ("the theory should generalize if possible") It does, at no extra cost. The R11 record in Lean is a joint step for any finite set of agents: what each believed the shared goal was, the part each played, what each saw of the others, and what each believed afterwards. That fits an episode where claude-4 starts a phase with several agents as well as a War Machine click with two. No theorem in the module depends on the number of agents; only its two worked controls use two.

㊢ ("one of my instructions might have gotten dropped") That case is already one of the controls I added from the dark-tower reading. The shared-state section asks that every shared item has exactly one writer, and it refuses two cases: both agents taking the item, and neither taking it because each thought it was the other's. A dropped instruction is the second case. The companion theorem says that when the agents agree on who has what, their shares add up to the whole, so nothing is dropped.

🈲 ("keep the implementation simple") For the War Machine I will hold R11 to this:
- **Agents:** the author and the reviewer, as named by `FUTON_WM_AUTHOR_AGENT` and `FUTON_WM_REVIEWER_AGENT` in `full_loop_runner.clj`.
- **Evidence:** read from records the run already holds. I will not add a model of other agents to the machine.
- **Check:** the two-agent case of the Lean record. The first question is the one-writer one: did the author write the artefact, did the reviewer write only the verdict, and was every part of the task taken by one of them.

㊟ (order of work, revised) I proposed rewriting the run-time census for all nodes and adding producers for R20 and R11. Against "get back to running experiments" that is too much at once. The precision restatement with codex-10 is worth finishing, because today a correct record from the code fails the Lean. After that I will take the nodes where the code already computes the right thing and only the check is missing, and leave R20 and anything wider on R11 until experiments are running again.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(first: what "compose coherently" means) The excursion's Q1 says pattern gluing refuses when a variable would get two mechanisms or when the result has a cycle, and identifies the first with Fritz and Liang's rule that every wire has exactly one driver. I read their Def. 3.6 myself and applied the same rule to agents on shared state: every shared variable has exactly one writer. The module now proves:
- **No-conflict:** agents who hold the same belief about who writes what give every variable exactly one writer.
- **Conservation:** under the same agreement, the agents' shares add up to the whole.
- **Controls:** two agents who each think the variable is theirs (two writers), and two who each think it is the other's (no writer), are both refused.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (resource conservation) I told you neither source gives a statement for it. Maisto still doesn't, but under the one-writer reading it has a statement, and it follows from agreement.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (second: the operator as one of the parties) The excursion's Q7 and zaif treat your preferences as something the agent infers from your messages. Maisto's second simulation is that asymmetric case: a "leader" who knows the goal takes a longer route because the short one "is equally likely if the intended goals are red or blue". R11 therefore covers operator and agent as well as seat and seat. The existing theorem that a move equally likely under every goal tells the observer nothing now cites that passage.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (third: silence) Q7 found that the record cannot tell a declined proposal from an unseen one, and that turn 392 was answered but not recorded. The codex-10 module had every agent observe a move at every step. I made the observation optional: with nothing observed the belief must stay where it was, and a record where it moved is refused.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (silence, limit) Silence can still depend on the answer, which is the excursion's self-masking case. Learning from it would need silence modelled as an observation with its own likelihood, and the module does not do that.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(where they differ) The excursion maps the stack onto category theory, and most of its rows are tagged as our mapping or underdetermined. The R11 module uses finite Bayes only and imports no Markov category.
- **Seam S19:** it asks whether any active-inference paper composes two agents, each the other's environment. Maisto does so concretely, though not categorically.
- **Policies as combs:** the reading where each agent's policy has a hole the other agent fills stays underdetermined there, and nothing in the module depends on it.

(review of `d84a603bba`) What I checked and changed:
- **Record:** two files, as asked; no `sorry`, `axiom` or `native_decide`; the build log is committed and passes.
- **`agreement_composes`:** it ignored its belief hypotheses and held by unfolding. It now takes the goals the agents select and uses certainty to conclude the joint action is the agreed goal.
- **One control:** it never mentioned the record. It is replaced by a theorem and control over the record's conformance.
- **Unused hypothesis:** removed from three theorems.
- **Header:** it now quotes the contract's R11.
- **Code answer:** codex-10 found no rebuilt model holding a belief about another agent or a shared goal. I checked only by a term search under `aif/wm` (no hits), not by reading the code.
